title: Top K Frequent Elements
statement: Return the `k` most frequent values in `nums`, ordered from most frequent to least frequent. If frequencies tie, the smaller value comes first.
constraints: k is in the range 1..number of unique values
hints: Count with a hash map first. The rest of the problem is selection on the counts.
A heap of size k keeps the current leaders in O(n log k).
Bucket sort by frequency is linear: bucket[count] holds every value that occurs count times.

approaches.name: Min-heap of size k
approaches.explanation: Push counts and pop the smallest when the heap exceeds k.

approaches.name: Frequency buckets
approaches.explanation: Index buckets by count and walk from the high end.

editorial: Frequency counting is mandatory and linear. Bucket sort then exploits the fact that a count is between 1 and n. Walk counts from n down to 1 and emit values until k of them have been produced. Sorting each bucket by value makes ties deterministic.

examples.explanation: 1 appears three times and 2 appears twice.
